GM SHEET • SETTLEMENT

THE FIRST NIGHT'S STORM

SP hub • shelter, supplies and a trapped voice

Student Player Log
Gate / Entry

GATE: 16 SP / 12 LP
ENTRY: -3 SP group, -1 LP group
No required role. Max 4 participants.

GM Opening — Read Aloud

The first real storm arrives before anyone is ready. Wind presses against the Settlement like a hand trying to flatten it. Tarps tear loose. Rain needles through gaps in the roofs. Then a crack splits the noise—not thunder, wood. One of the outer shelters is folding inward. There are supplies inside, and at least one person shouting from somewhere in the dark. This is the Settlement's first test: protect what keeps people alive, but do not forget there are people inside the walls.

Group Roster
CharacterRoleSpecialtyWeaknessLPSP
DiannaScavengerPhysicalEmotion47
Kael MorenoScavengerPhysicalEmotion47
Celia LintonCaretakerIntelligencePhysical65
Dillon GoldbergLeaderPhysicalCreative66
Isla CarterCaretakerIntelligenceCreative65
Mission Stages

1. HOLD THE FRAME

Who should be assigned to hold the collapsing frame? This is a Physical action.

The shelter shudders as you reach it. A main beam has split and the whole left side sags with every blast of wind. To hold it, someone has to step under the weight and brace the frame long enough for the others to move. It is ugly, direct work: cold rain, splinters, muscle and nerve. Choose carefully: this person cannot take another stage later.

Trait tested: Physical • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe beam drops hard. You keep it from crushing the shelter, but it takes something out of you.
3–4-1 SP selfYou hold it, but only barely. Your arms shake by the end.
5–6+1 SP SettlementYou find the right angle. The frame locks into place long enough to save the structure.

2. SAVE THE FOOD

Who should be assigned to sort and save the exposed supplies? This is an Intelligence action.

Inside, everything is scattered. Grain has spilled across a wet floor. Crates are cracked open. Some food is already mixing with mud and rainwater. The wrong choice wastes time and ruins supplies; the right choice buys the whole Settlement another day. Someone needs to think quickly, sort what can be saved and decide what must be abandoned.

Trait tested: Intelligence • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP SettlementToo much is contaminated before you can organize it.
3–4No changeYou save enough to prevent disaster, but nothing more.
5–6+2 SP SettlementYou recover more than expected and store it properly.

3. THE VOICE IN THE WALL

Who should be assigned to decide what to do about the trapped person? This is an Emotion action.

A voice breaks through the wind: someone is pinned behind a collapsed section of wall. At the same time, another stack of supplies begins sliding toward the opening. You cannot personally handle both. This is not only a rescue; it is a test of what the Settlement becomes when fear and need collide. Someone must choose how to act while everyone else watches.

Trait tested: Emotion • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP selfYou hesitate or act coldly. The person survives, but something human is damaged.
3–4-1 LP selfYou help, but the moment leaves a mark.
5–6+2 LP group poolYou make the human choice clearly. People remember it.
Role Triggers / Post-Mission

• Scavenger trigger: if a stage includes searching/salvage, roll 1d6 for +SP exactly as role states. • Caretaker trigger: if someone loses SP, reduce SP loss by 1 or cancel one consequence. • Leader trigger: if Dillon takes control, +2 to one roll; if it fails, every participant loses -1 SP. POST: +2 SP total to assign to players or Settlement. If Settlement ends with any stage success, +1 LP Settlement for surviving the storm together. Role bonuses apply only when their trigger happens. Specialty/weakness doubles resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

THE DOOR THAT STILL KNOWS NAMES

LP hub • locked systems, lost people and dangerous salvage

Student Player Log
Gate / Entry

GATE: 18 SP / 8 LP
ENTRY: -2 SP group, -2 LP group
No required role. Max 4 participants.

GM Opening — Read Aloud

Past the dead escalators, behind a staff-only door, the Terminal still has one working system: an old directory screen flickering through names, gate numbers and fragments of delayed flights from the day the world ended. The door to the control room is locked, but the screen keeps refreshing like it is waiting for someone to answer. This place does not need strength alone. It needs someone to decide whether the past is junk, evidence or a message.

Group Roster
CharacterRoleSpecialtyWeaknessLPSP
Amber RoseScavengerPhysicalCreative47
Kai AndersonScavengerPhysicalCreative47
Aaron JonesScavengerPhysicalIntelligence47
Tyler VegasCaretakerIntelligenceEmotion65
Mission Stages

1. OPEN THE STAFF DOOR

Who should be assigned to force or finesse the staff door open? This is a Physical action.

The door is heavy, reinforced and swollen in its frame. The lock is old, but not dead. You can pry it, shoulder it, jam it, kick it or find another way through. Every method makes noise. Every method uses strength. Behind the door, the directory screen flashes another list of names.

Trait tested: Physical • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe door gives suddenly and you take the impact.
3–4-1 SP selfIt opens, but it costs you.
5–6+1 SP group poolYou open it cleanly and keep momentum.

2. READ THE SYSTEM

Who should be assigned to understand the directory controls? This is an Intelligence action.

The control room smells like dust and hot plastic. The directory system is still running, but barely. Half the keys stick. Some names repeat. Some routes make no sense anymore. Someone has to decide what the machine is actually telling you before the screen burns out.

Trait tested: Intelligence • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP TerminalYou erase or scramble part of the directory.
3–4No changeYou understand enough to move on.
5–6+2 LP TerminalYou preserve a clean list of names and destinations.

3. CHOOSE THE NAMES

Who should be assigned to decide what names to copy, speak or save? This is Emotion OR Creative.

The screen shows hundreds of names. Most mean nothing to you. That is what makes it hard. These were people going somewhere. Families, workers, strangers, children, someone expected at an arrival gate. You cannot save every name before the system fades. Someone has to choose how to honor what remains.

Trait tested: Emotion or Creative • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP selfThe names become noise. You shut something off inside yourself.
3–4+1 LP TerminalYou save a few names and the room feels less empty.
5–6+2 LP Terminal, +1 LP groupYou turn the list into memory, not data.

OPTIONAL. RAID LOST-AND-FOUND

Does someone search lost-and-found before leaving? This triggers Scavenger. Physical action if forced, Intelligence if careful.

On the way out, you spot the lost-and-found cage. Bags, coats, chargers, toys, medicine cases—little leftovers of ordinary life. Searching it could help everyone. It could also feel like stealing from ghosts. The cage is stuck, and time is thinning.

Trait tested: Physical or Intelligence • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe cage collapses inward while you search.
3–4+1 SP selfYou find one useful thing.
5–6+2 SP self, +1 LP TerminalYou find supplies and preserve one meaningful object.
Role Triggers / Post-Mission

• Scavenger trigger: Amber, Kai or Aaron may use Scavenger during lost-and-found or search moments. • Caretaker trigger: Tyler may reduce SP loss by 1 or cancel one consequence when harm occurs. • Special warning: several Terminal actions test Creative/Emotion; the group is strong in SP but must protect LP. POST: +2 LP total to assign. If optional search succeeds, +1 SP Terminal. Role bonuses apply only when their trigger happens. Specialty/weakness doubles resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

GM SHEET • HIGHWAY COLONY

THE OVERPASS GAP

SP hub • movement, repair and frightened witnesses

Student Player Log
Gate / Entry

GATE: 15 SP / 10 LP
ENTRY: -3 SP group, -1 LP group
Requires Builder OR Leader. Max 4 participants.

GM Opening — Read Aloud

The Highway Colony stops at a broken overpass where the road has fallen away into a narrow concrete gap. The convoy cannot turn around; too many people, too much weight, too little daylight. A rusted bus lies half across the break like an accidental bridge. People stare at it, afraid to trust it and afraid not to. If the Colony cannot move, it becomes a target. If it moves badly, people fall.

Group Roster
CharacterRoleSpecialtyWeaknessLPSP
BlairLeaderIntelligenceEmotion56
AzrielHistorianIntelligenceEmotion56
Ryker StoneBuilderPhysicalEmotion57
Sunshine StarScavengerCreativePhysical55
Mission Stages

1. READ THE ROAD

Who should be assigned to inspect the gap and plan the crossing? This is an Intelligence action.

From a distance, the bus looks useful. Up close, it looks like a mistake waiting to happen. The pavement around it is cracked, the angle is wrong, and the underside has rusted through in places. Someone has to read the whole scene: where weight can go, where wheels should not, where people should stand and where fear is lying to them.

Trait tested: Intelligence • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP Highway ColonyThe plan misses a weak point. The route becomes more dangerous for everyone.
3–4No changeYou find a workable path, but it is tight.
5–6+1 SP Highway ColonyYou spot the safest route and mark it clearly.

2. BRACE THE BUS

Who should be assigned to brace or stabilize the bus? This is a Physical action. Builder may trigger if Ryker handles or supports this stage.

The bus groans when anyone steps near it. To make it usable, someone has to wedge debris beneath the frame, hammer loose metal into place and trust their hands more than their fear. The work is loud enough that people stop arguing and start watching. If this brace holds, the Colony moves. If not, the road breaks under them.

Trait tested: Physical • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe brace slips and you take the hit.
3–4-1 SP selfIt holds, but you pay for it physically.
5–6+2 SP Highway ColonyThe brace sets firm. The crossing becomes possible.

3. MAKE THEM CROSS

Who should be assigned to convince the frightened travelers to move? This is an Emotion action.

The structure is ready, but the people are not. A younger traveler refuses to step onto the bus. Others begin backing away. Panic moves faster than orders. Someone has to speak to them as people, not cargo: calm them, steady them and make the first step feel possible. This is where the road becomes a community or a crowd.

Trait tested: Emotion • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP selfYour words make things worse. Fear spreads.
3–4No changeThey cross, but they do not trust you more for it.
5–6+2 LP group poolThey follow because you make them believe they can.

OPTIONAL. SEARCH THE BUS

After the main crossing, does someone search the bus? This triggers Scavenger if Sunshine acts. This is Creative OR Physical depending on method.

Once the first people cross, you see something under a seat: a sealed emergency case, wedged behind twisted metal. Taking it means slowing the convoy and entering the unstable bus after everyone already decided it was dangerous. Leave it and you keep moving. Reach for it and maybe the road gives you a gift.

Trait tested: Physical or Creative • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe bus shifts while you reach inside.
3–4+1 SP selfYou pull out something useful, but small.
5–6+2 SP self, +1 SP HighwayYou recover a real emergency kit.
Role Triggers / Post-Mission

• Builder trigger: after successful brace/crossing, Ryker may add +2 SP or +2 LP to Highway Colony. • Historian trigger: Azriel may prevent up to 2 LP loss if the group frames the crossing through memory of how roads once connected people. • Leader trigger: Blair may take control for +2 to one roll; failure costs all participants -1 SP. • Scavenger trigger: Sunshine may roll scavenger effect during the optional search. POST: +2 SP total to assign. If Stage 3 succeeds, +1 LP Highway Colony. Role bonuses apply only when their trigger happens. Specialty/weakness doubles resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

THE FIRELIT AUDITION

LP hub • identity, repair and proof of worth

Student Player Log
Gate / Entry

GATE: 11 SP / 16 LP
ENTRY: -1 SP group, -3 LP group
Requires Leader OR Builder. Max 4 participants.

GM Opening — Read Aloud

The Caravan reaches a roadside camp just before dusk. The people there do not threaten you. They do something worse: they judge you. Their fire is clean, their weapons visible, their faces unreadable. They have seen desperate groups, violent groups, charming groups and useless groups. A woman near the fire says, 'We trade with people who will still be people next month.' Tonight, the Caravan has to prove it is more than motion.

Group Roster
CharacterRoleSpecialtyWeaknessLPSP
AnnieCaretakerIntelligenceEmotion65
SarinaCaretakerIntelligenceEmotion65
Fox RavewoodLeaderIntelligencePhysical65
Jax HarlanBuilderPhysicalIntelligence57
Mission Stages

1. SAY WHO YOU ARE

Who should be assigned to speak for the Caravan? This is an Intelligence OR Emotion action. Leader may trigger if Fox takes control.

The camp quiets and gives you the full weight of its attention. This is not a speech contest. They are listening for contradictions: brave words with selfish eyes, promises with no plan, beauty with no backbone. Someone has to define the Caravan in a way that sounds like a future, not an excuse.

Trait tested: Intelligence or Emotion • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP selfYour answer sounds hollow. They hear survival, but not legacy.
3–4-1 LP selfThey listen, but they are not convinced yet.
5–6+2 LP group poolYou give them a reason to keep listening.

2. FIX WHAT THEY WON'T

Who should be assigned to repair the broken cook-frame by the fire? This is a Physical action. Builder may trigger if Jax handles it.

A metal cook-frame beside the fire has collapsed. They mention it casually, but it is a test. Anyone can claim they are useful; fewer can make something useful with cold hands and everyone watching. The repair will not win their love, but it might prove the Caravan leaves places better than it found them.

Trait tested: Physical • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 SP selfThe frame snaps back and cuts into you.
3–4No changeYou patch it enough to function.
5–6+2 SP CaravanThe repair is solid. Practical trust begins.

3. WHAT DO YOU OFFER?

Who should be assigned to offer a meaningful artifact, story or service? This is Emotion OR Creative.

The woman by the fire nods toward what you carry. 'Not payment,' she says. 'Proof.' They want to see whether anything still matters to you. You can offer an object, a story, a skill, a promise or a performance. But whatever you offer has to cost something emotionally, or it will not count.

Trait tested: Emotion or Creative • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-2 LP selfThe offering feels false or forced. You lose face.
3–4+1 LP CaravanIt matters enough to be accepted.
5–6+2 LP Caravan, +1 LP selfThey understand what you are carrying forward.

OPTIONAL. TEND THE BURNED HAND

A child burns their hand near the fire. Does a Caretaker step in? This is Intelligence. Caretaker trigger applies if Annie or Sarina acts.

Just as the test seems finished, a child knocks a kettle sideways and screams. No one asks you to help. That is the point. Helping will slow the negotiation and expose you to judgment if you fail. Ignoring it keeps the mission clean. The camp notices either way.

Trait tested: Intelligence • Specialty/weakness doubles the resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

RollResultNarration
1–2-1 SP self, -1 LP CaravanYou make the injury worse and the camp pulls back.
3–4+1 LP CaravanYou help enough to matter.
5–6+2 LP CaravanThe child calms. So does the camp.
Role Triggers / Post-Mission

• Caretaker trigger: Annie/Sarina may reduce SP loss by 1 or cancel one consequence when harm occurs. • Leader trigger: Fox may take control for +2 to one roll; failure costs all participants -1 SP. • Builder trigger: Jax may add +2 SP or +2 LP to Caravan after a successful mission. POST: +3 LP total to assign. If Stage 2 succeeds, +1 SP Caravan. Role bonuses apply only when their trigger happens. Specialty/weakness doubles resulting SP/LP gain or loss.

MISSION TWO • HIGHWAY COLONY + TERMINAL

THE DOORS BETWEEN

Stage One is fast survival combat. Stage Two splits into private, password-locked briefings so each group can study the opposing community and vote on a posture before the joint first-contact turn.

← Home
Quick Combat Rules

ROLL ONE D6 WHEN YOUR CHARACTER ACTS

1: you take the listed SP loss. 2–3: you fend off danger for one turn. 4–5: you defeat the attacker on you. 6: you defeat yours and help one ally defeat theirs.

Specialty: +1 if your action clearly uses your specialty. Weakness: -1 if your action clearly relies on your weakness. Rolls cannot go below 1 or above 6.

ROLE MOVES: USE ONCE PER FIGHT

Leader: give one ally +1. Caretaker: cancel 1 SP loss. Builder: turn one 2–3 into a 4. Scavenger: find an improvised weapon or route; +1 to one roll. Historian: remember an old-world pattern; reroll one failed Intelligence action. Artist/Performer: distract, signal or steady the group; give one ally +1 or cancel 1 SP loss.

STAGE ONE: Separate Attack Encounters

HIGHWAY COLONY ATTACK: WOLVES ON THE OVERPASS

Main risk: SP loss. This is about surviving the road.

The convoy slows under a buckled overpass where abandoned cars narrow the road. At first, the shapes moving between the vehicles look like shadows. Then the growling begins. A pack of starving wolves spills from beneath the ramp, fast enough to split the group and smart enough to go for the youngest travelers first.

The buses cannot move until someone clears the road. Every character chooses one action: fight, climb, distract, protect an NPC, fix the bus path, scare the pack or use an item.

RollResultWhat happens
1-2 SP selfThe wolf gets through your guard. You survive, but the road takes blood.
2–3No changeYou keep the wolf back for one turn. You are still locked in.
4–5+1 SP group poolYou drive off or defeat the wolf attacking you. The convoy gains ground.
6+1 SP group poolYou defeat yours and help an ally. The group sees you as someone who keeps people alive.

TERMINAL ATTACK: DOGS IN BAGGAGE CLAIM

Main risk: SP loss. This is about keeping bodies alive before arguing about rules.

The Terminal has kept the lower baggage tunnels sealed for years. During the storm, one rusted gate finally gives. Feral airport dogs pour into the claim area, slipping over old suitcases and under security tape. They are not evil. They are hungry. That makes the choice worse.

Terminal characters must defend the doors without letting panic overrun the building. Choose one action: hold a barricade, lure the dogs away, protect a child, improvise a trap, calm panic, treat a wound or open a controlled escape route.

RollResultWhat happens
1-2 SP selfA dog breaks through your space. You survive, but you are hurt or someone near you is hurt.
2–3No changeYou hold your position for one turn. The doors remain contested.
4–5+1 SP Terminal poolYou drive off the dog attacking your area and keep the space intact.
6+1 SP Terminal poolYou save your area and help someone else. The Terminal holds.
Fast Roll Tracker
PlayerGroupActionRollSP +/-Note
STAGE TWO: Private Briefings

The Highway Colony reaches the airport carrying injuries, fear and pride. The Terminal has just survived its own breach. Neither group is calm. Neither group is ready to trust. Before they meet, each side studies what it knows and votes on a posture: Friendly, Trade, Secretive or Hostile.

Highway Colony Private Briefing

Locked. Highway reads about the Terminal, considers benefits/risks and votes on a posture.

Open Highway Briefing

Terminal Private Briefing

Locked. Terminal reads about the Highway Colony, considers benefits/risks and votes on a posture.

Open Terminal Briefing
STAGE TWO: Joint First Contact
Share Postures, Take Individual Turns

How This Round Works

  1. Finish private group meetings first. Each group opens its locked briefing, discusses the other community and votes on one posture: Friendly, Trade, Secretive or Hostile.
  2. Share postures with the other group. Write both group postures in the chart below, then check the combo table for the overall scene vibe.
  3. Take individual turns. Each player chooses one action from their group posture. Say what your character actually does in the scene, then roll 1d6.
  4. Use one Specialty and one Role only if they fit. Matching Specialty = +1. Matching Weakness = -1. Listed Role with an explanation = +1. Keep it quick.

Roll bands after modifiers: 1 or lower = Failure. 2–3 = Hold the line. 4–5 = Success. 6 or higher = Critical success.

Specialties: Physical, Intelligence, Emotion, Creative. Roles: Leader, Caretaker, Builder, Scavenger, Historian, Artist, Performer.

1. Record Group Postures
GroupPosture

Terminal Posture:

Each player fills one row. The action should be concrete and narrative: “I try to make friends with the guard,” “I quietly search the wagon,” “I step between my group and theirs,” “I challenge our leader before someone gets hurt.” Then roll and record what happens.

4. Action Cards by Posture

FRIENDLY

Goal: build trust without getting careless.

A. Offer help to one specific person

Best fit: Emotion. Helpful roles: Caretaker, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerYour help exposes someone to danger or humiliation. Lose -1 SP if someone gets endangered, or -1 LP if trust turns ugly.
2–3You help cautiously. No point change; the other side notices but does not fully trust you.
4–5Your help clearly matters to one person. Gain +1 LP.
6+Your help changes the whole meeting. Gain +1 LP and give one ally +1 on their roll.

B. Start a real conversation

Best fit: Emotion or Creative. Helpful roles: Artist, Performer, Historian.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou say the wrong thing or sound fake. Lose -1 LP.
2–3The conversation happens, but stays guarded. No point change.
4–5You create a personal connection. Gain +1 LP.
6+Someone on the other side genuinely likes or trusts you. Gain +1 LP and ask one honest question.

C. Protect someone vulnerable

Best fit: Physical or Emotion. Helpful roles: Caretaker, Builder.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou step in too late or in the wrong way. Lose -1 SP.
2–3You prevent immediate harm. No point change.
4–5You protect someone and look reliable. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP.
6+You protect someone and create trust. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP, and give that person +1 on their next roll.

D. Warn your group not to overtrust

Best fit: Intelligence. Helpful roles: Leader, Historian, Scavenger.

RollResult
1 or lowerYour caution becomes paranoia. Lose -1 LP.
2–3Your warning is heard but changes little. No point change.
4–5You set a useful boundary. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP.
6+You spot a real risk before it matters. Gain +1 SP and give one ally +1.

TRADE

Goal: exchange value without turning people into supplies.

A. Make a fair offer

Best fit: Intelligence or Creative. Helpful roles: Leader, Scavenger, Artist, Performer.

RollResult
1 or lowerYour offer insults them or reveals need. Lose -1 LP.
2–3The offer is understood, but no one moves yet. No point change.
4–5The offer creates a workable exchange. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP.
6+The deal gives both sides a reason to continue. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP and give one ally +1.

B. Inspect their offer for danger

Best fit: Intelligence. Helpful roles: Scavenger, Historian, Builder.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou accuse too quickly or miss the real danger. Lose -1 LP.
2–3You see possible risk, but cannot prove it. No point change.
4–5You catch a real problem before it hurts anyone. Gain +1 SP.
6+You catch the problem and suggest a better deal. Gain +1 SP and ask them to revise one term.

C. Hold back one valuable thing

Best fit: Intelligence or Emotion. Helpful roles: Scavenger, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerThey notice you are hiding leverage. Lose -1 LP.
2–3You keep it hidden but gain nothing yet. No point change.
4–5You preserve leverage for the next exchange. Gain +1 SP.
6+You preserve leverage and learn what they need. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP and give one ally +1.

D. Sweeten the deal to prevent conflict

Best fit: Creative or Emotion. Helpful roles: Artist, Performer, Caretaker, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou look desperate or manipulative. Lose -1 SP or -1 LP.
2–3The sweetener delays conflict but does not solve it. No point change.
4–5The added offer calms the meeting. Gain +1 LP.
6+The deal becomes a bridge instead of a transaction. Gain +1 LP and give one ally +1.

SECRETIVE

Goal: protect secrets without letting paranoia run the scene.

A. Hide your group’s weakest point

Best fit: Intelligence or Physical. Helpful roles: Scavenger, Builder, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerThe lie or cover is obvious. Lose -1 LP.
2–3The weakness stays hidden for now. No point change.
4–5You protect the weak point and buy time. Gain +1 SP.
6+You turn the weakness into an advantage. Gain +1 SP and give one ally +1.

B. Investigate quietly

Best fit: Intelligence or Physical. Helpful roles: Scavenger, Historian.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou are caught spying or prying. Lose -1 LP.
2–3You notice something unclear. No point change.
4–5You learn one useful truth. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP.
6+You learn a useful truth and a hidden pressure. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP and ask one pointed question.

C. Leak one truth to build trust

Best fit: Emotion. Helpful roles: Historian, Caretaker, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou reveal truth to the wrong person or at the wrong time. Lose -1 LP.
2–3The truth lands, but changes little. No point change.
4–5The truth makes you more believable. Gain +1 LP.
6+The truth creates a private bond across groups. Gain +1 LP and cancel one ally’s LP loss this turn.

D. Cover for an ally who is lying badly

Best fit: Creative or Emotion. Helpful roles: Performer, Artist, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou make the lie worse. Lose -1 LP, and that ally cannot use a bonus this turn.
2–3You keep the lie from collapsing. No point change.
4–5You stabilize the story. Gain +1 LP.
6+You turn a bad lie into a useful half-truth. Gain +1 LP and give that ally +1.

HOSTILE

Goal: survive the standoff without making violence the only language.

A. Fight with your group

Best fit: Physical. Helpful roles: Leader, Builder, Scavenger.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou escalate too far and someone gets hurt. Lose -1 SP and -1 LP.
2–3You hold position. No point change, but the standoff continues.
4–5You force them to back up without losing control. Gain +1 SP.
6+You win space and keep your group coordinated. Gain +1 SP and give one ally +1.

B. Rebel and try to stop violence

Best fit: Emotion or Physical. Helpful roles: Caretaker, Leader.

RollResult
1 or lowerYour own group turns on you or ignores you. Lose -1 LP.
2–3You slow the violence but do not stop it. No point change.
4–5You prevent one person from getting hurt. Gain +1 LP.
6+You break the standoff for one turn. Gain +1 LP and cancel one ally’s SP loss this turn.

C. Make peace from inside the standoff

Best fit: Emotion or Intelligence. Helpful roles: Historian, Leader, Performer.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou look like a traitor to one side and weak to the other. Lose -1 LP.
2–3You create a pause, but not a solution. No point change.
4–5You de-escalate one immediate threat. Gain +1 LP.
6+You change the tone of the standoff. Gain +1 LP and give one ally +1 on a nonviolent action.

D. Intimidate without attacking

Best fit: Physical or Creative. Helpful roles: Performer, Leader, Builder.

RollResult
1 or lowerYou overplay it. Someone panics or challenges you. Lose -1 SP or -1 LP.
2–3You create silence, not trust. No point change.
4–5You gain space without starting a fight. Gain +1 SP.
6+You force a pause and make violence less likely. Gain +1 SP or +1 LP and give one ally +1.

MISSION TWO • CARAVAN + SETTLEMENT

THE NIGHT OF BREAD AND MUSIC

Stage One is fast survival combat. Stage Two splits into private, password-locked briefings so each group can study the opposing community and vote on a posture before the joint first-contact turn.

← Home
Quick Combat Rules

ROLL ONE D6 WHEN YOUR CHARACTER ACTS

1: you take the listed SP loss. 2–3: you fend off danger for one turn. 4–5: you defeat the attacker on you. 6: you defeat yours and help one ally defeat theirs.

Specialty: +1 if your action clearly uses your specialty. Weakness: -1 if your action clearly relies on your weakness. Rolls cannot go below 1 or above 6.

ROLE MOVES: USE ONCE PER FIGHT

Leader: give one ally +1. Caretaker: cancel 1 SP loss. Builder: turn one 2–3 into a 4. Scavenger: find an improvised weapon or route; +1 to one roll. Historian: remember an old-world pattern; reroll one failed Intelligence action. Artist/Performer: distract, signal or steady the group; give one ally +1 or cancel 1 SP loss.

STAGE ONE: Separate Attack Encounters

CARAVAN ATTACK: WOLVES BEYOND THE FIRELIGHT

Main risk: SP loss. Art matters, but first the fire has to hold.

The Caravan is rehearsing beside the road when the horses go silent. Then the wolves appear beyond the firelight: first two, then five, then too many to count cleanly. They do not attack the strongest people first. They circle the props, instruments and children, looking for fear.

The Caravan can survive by fighting, but it can also survive by staying Caravan: noise, rhythm, signal fires, coordinated movement, tricks, stories and nerve. Choose one action: fight, distract, protect, lead, use an instrument, use a prop, light the dark or pull someone back from panic.

RollResultWhat happens
1-2 SP selfThe wolf gets inside the circle. You are knocked down, bitten or forced to spend the turn saving yourself.
2–3No changeYou hold your wolf off for one turn. The firelight still belongs to you.
4–5+1 SP Caravan poolYou drive off the wolf attacking you and keep the road open.
6+1 SP Caravan poolYou defeat yours and help an ally. For one second, the fight becomes choreography.

SETTLEMENT ATTACK: RAIDERS AT THE FENCE

Main risk: SP loss. This is about defending food, water and people.

The Settlement hears the warning bell before sunset. Figures move between the trees near the garden fence: hungry raiders with hooks, clubs and old plastic shields. They are not a full army, but they know exactly what the Settlement has. Food. Water. People who are used to sleeping behind walls.

The Settlement must defend the fence without turning into nothing but a fence. Choose one action: hold the line, protect a child, repair a breach, scare them off, negotiate, set a trap, move supplies or help someone who falls.

RollResultWhat happens
1-2 SP selfThe fence breaks near you, or someone gets hurt because you were too slow.
2–3No changeYou hold your section for one turn. The pressure continues.
4–5+1 SP Settlement poolYou push back the attacker on you and keep your section standing.
6+1 SP Settlement poolYou stop your attacker and help an ally without forgetting who you are defending.

PlayerGroupActionRollSP +/-Note
STAGE TWO: Private Briefings

The Caravan arrives carrying smoke, tooth-marks and the stubborn urge to make the road mean something. The Settlement has just defended its fence and counted what the attack almost cost. Before bread is shared or songs are played, each side studies what it knows and votes on a posture: Friendly, Trade, Secretive or Hostile.

Caravan Private Briefing

Locked. Caravan reads about the Settlement, considers benefits/risks and votes on a posture.

STAGE TWO: Joint First Contact
Share Postures, Take Individual Turns

How This Round Works

  1. Finish private group meetings first. Each group opens its locked briefing, discusses the other community and votes on one posture: Friendly, Trade, Secretive or Hostile.
  2. Share postures with the other group. Write both group postures in the chart below, then check the combo table for the overall scene vibe.
  3. Take individual turns. Each player chooses one action from their group posture. Say what your character actually does in the scene, then roll 1d6.
  4. Use one Specialty and one Role only if they fit. Matching Specialty = +1. Matching Weakness = -1. Listed Role with an explanation = +1. Keep it quick.

Roll bands after modifiers: 1 or lower = Failure. 2–3 = Hold the line. 4–5 = Success. 6 or higher = Critical success.

Specialties: Physical, Intelligence, Emotion, Creative. Roles: Leader, Caretaker, Builder, Scavenger, Historian, Artist, Performer.

1. Record Group Postures
GroupPosture
Caravan Posture:
Settlement Posture:
2. Combo Vibe
Posture ComboScene VibeWhat the turn is testing
Friendly + FriendlyRelief, maybe too much trust too fast.Can kindness become real without becoming careless?
Friendly + TradeOne side offers humanity; the other asks for terms.Can a deal avoid making generosity feel stupid?
Friendly + SecretiveWarmth meets withheld truth.Does secrecy protect people or poison trust?
Friendly + HostileOne open hand, one raised weapon.Can anyone prevent fear from controlling the meeting?
Trade + TradeClear-eyed bargaining.Can both groups get value without reducing people to supplies?
Trade + SecretiveLeverage, suspicion and half-truths.Who can make a useful deal without getting played?
Trade + HostileA bargain under threat.Is this trade, extortion or the beginning of an alliance?
Secretive + SecretiveEveryone is hiding something.Can one honest opening appear before paranoia wins?
Secretive + HostilePressure meets secrets.Can exposure happen without turning into violence?
Hostile + HostileImmediate standoff.Will someone win, break the pattern or make everything worse?

Each player fills one row. The action should be concrete and narrative: “I try to make friends with the guard,” “I quietly search the wagon,” “I step between my group and theirs,” “I challenge our leader before someone gets hurt.” Then roll and record what happens.

MISSION TWO • PRIVATE BRIEFING

Highway Colony Briefing: Studying the Terminal

Password locked so the other group cannot casually read your prep. Read, discuss, vote on posture, then return to the joint mission page.

← Home

Enter passphrase

Enter your group passphrase. Capitalization does not matter.

What You See
The airport is not abandoned. Light moves behind the glass. People watch from behind barricades made of luggage carts and broken security gates. You can smell old carpet, rainwater and something almost impossible: medicine. The Terminal looks like a place that survived by staying still and making rules.

Possible Benefits

  • Shelter from the storm and maybe a place to sleep without engines running.
  • Possible medicine, maps, tools and old-world supplies.
  • A stable place where sick or young NPCs might recover.
  • A chance to learn what staying still costs.

Possible Dangers

  • They may lock you out, separate you or demand names before help.
  • They may have more supplies than they admit.
  • Their rules could trap your people or split the convoy.
  • If you look weak, they may decide you need managing.

Questions You Should Ask

  • What will we ask for first?
  • What injury, number or weakness should we hide?
  • Are we entering as guests, traders, scouts or threats?
  • Who in our group might want to stay?

MISSION TWO • PRIVATE BRIEFING

Terminal Briefing: Studying the Highway Colony

Password locked so the other group cannot casually read your prep. Read, discuss, vote on posture, then return to the joint mission page.

← Home

Enter passphrase

Enter your group passphrase. Capitalization does not matter.

What You See
The convoy appears out of the storm like a moving town: buses, patched vehicles, armed adults, tired children and people who know how to sleep with one eye open. They are not raiders, exactly. They are not safe, either. The Highway Colony looks like a group that survived by never letting the world hold still around them.

Possible Benefits

  • They know roads, threats, routes and what has happened beyond the airport.
  • They may bring trade goods, labor, repairs or protection.
  • They could help the Terminal stop becoming a museum with locked doors.
  • Their movement may connect you to other living communities.

Possible Dangers

  • Raiders, sickness or conflict may have followed them.
  • They may refuse your rules, especially names and entry limits.
  • They may steal supplies if desperation wins.
  • Your own young people may envy their freedom.

Questions You Should Ask

  • What must we know before opening the doors?
  • What will we offer before asking questions?
  • Which rule matters most, and which rule can bend?
  • Who in our group might want to leave?

MISSION TWO • PRIVATE BRIEFING

Caravan Briefing: Studying the Settlement

Password locked so the other group cannot casually read your prep. Read, discuss, vote on posture, then return to the joint mission page.

← Home

Enter passphrase

Enter your group passphrase. Capitalization does not matter.

What You See
The Settlement sits beside the lake with smoke from cookfires, garden rows, a fence that has just been tested and people who look at the road like it is both a promise and a disease. You can smell bread. You can also see watchful adults counting how many mouths you brought.

Possible Benefits

  • Food, water, repair materials and real rest.
  • A hungry audience for news, songs, stories and proof that the world continues.
  • Possible new members, especially restless young people.
  • A chance to make art useful, not decorative.

Possible Dangers

  • They may treat you like beggars, corruptors or extra mouths.
  • Their safety may tempt your people to stop moving.
  • They may demand labor before hospitality.
  • They may blame you for any danger that follows the road.

Questions You Should Ask

  • Do we perform first, trade first or ask plainly?
  • What loss or weakness from the attack should we hide?
  • Who might want to stay?
  • What can we offer that is not just entertainment?

MISSION TWO • PRIVATE BRIEFING

Settlement Briefing: Studying the Caravan

Password locked so the other group cannot casually read your prep. Read, discuss, vote on posture, then return to the joint mission page.

← Home

Enter passphrase

Enter your group passphrase. Capitalization does not matter.

What You See
The Caravan arrives with patched wagons, bright cloth, props, instruments and people who seem to carry another version of life with them. They are tired and hungry. They are also magnetic. After the attack at the fence, your people know what disorder can cost. But when the music reaches the gate, even the tired children look up.

Possible Benefits

  • They bring news, trade, repairs, stories and skills from the road.
  • They might help defend, scout or connect the Settlement to others.
  • Their art could remind people why survival is not enough.
  • They may offer young people a controlled way to imagine the world beyond the fence.

Possible Dangers

  • They may steal food, lure people away or disrupt routines.
  • They may be hiding injuries, hunger or danger behind performance.
  • Restless teenagers may see the Caravan as escape.
  • Hospitality could become obligation.

Questions You Should Ask

  • What can we offer without risking everyone?
  • What do we need from them besides entertainment?
  • Who must not be allowed to make promises alone?
  • Will we treat leaving as betrayal or choice?
